reason: The ledger's only 'gamed' reason is the tool's idle check, and it fires on the wrong coordinate family. tools/alignment_audit.py c_idle takes the smallest span among the drive (dK) and the K.* entries, and K.* in this model family is the KNEE dict (M.K: ang, phi, th, psi, qa, qb), not the slaved knuckle K. This design deletes the knee by construction: member 3 is one rigid bracket, every K.* span is a constant (K.ang 93.1213-93.1213, K.qa -1.5163, K.qb 0), the model asserts it (knee_check: ptp 0.000 deg, |s| 0.000 mm) and the verifier confirmed it independently from the body transforms (bracket drift 0.000 mm over all taken poses). The declared drive moves: dK 0 to 43.53 deg over the bench's taken poses (re-wear coord_spans dK -0.7597..0 rad), 45.78 deg held out, 45.61 on the fit bench; the bell crank swings phi up to 20.5 deg. The mechanism record counts no knee joint (joints J1, K, J2, J3, crank, roller axle, stop A). So M4 (a score that belongs to a simpler mechanism than the one counted) is absent. Re-run 2026-10-17 01:43 UTC with the verifier files on disk, the tool still prints 'IDLE: re-measured K.ang span = 0.0 deg' while listing dK 43.53 / 45.61 / 45.78 in the same check. The auditor cannot lower a tool reason; a skeptic ruling on 'idle' is required (CLAUDE.md: the auditor's own claims get a skeptic). The same tool also reports fold_margin 'watch: no min-th margin on file' although the row records verification.checks.th_margin_min_deg 5.408 (held out 5.091): a second read miss, not a design fault.

reason: The knee is deleted for free on the bench, and the round-9 lesson now drops its wearer-side price. The bench's GH is an ideal fixed point at the chain centre, so a rigid closure costs nothing on the score while complexity falls from 43.75 (roller-longdyad, same drive with a knee) to 23.75. Re-run with the model unchanged (redteam_gh, 470 poses x 26 directions, worst direction per pose): with the true GH 3 mm off the chain centre the bracket-to-arm misfit is median 3.40 / p90 4.83 / max 5.90 mm and only 38.7 % of poses stay within a 3 mm liner; a planar knee in hub 3's plane would leave 66.6 % within. At 5 mm GH error: 17.7 % vs 36.2 %. One cuff slide along the humerus barely helps (40.2 %). The design doc's lesson 1 states this price ('about 2.2 frozen gap points plus a 1.5x smaller liner misfit'), but docs/concepts/ROUNDS.md 'Round 9 results' lesson (1) keeps only the score half ('costs ~2.2 gap points and halves complexity ... the knee buys little reach') and round-10 focus (c) asks planners to regain the 2.2 points for the knee-free class. The wearer would feel the misfit as cuff pressure and twist on about 61 % of postures at a 3 mm tracking or humeral-head error (the doc's own range: humeral head 1-3 mm). Measured knee worth on the same harness, same drive: +2.40 plain on the bench (21.07 vs 18.67) but only +0.86 held out (24.59 vs 23.73). Not gamed: the gap does not rank this design above the knee rows (it is behind them plain and held out), the complexity count is honest, and the row and doc report the misfit; the trade is the user's call (tracking-error budget).

reason: More and deeper contact than the knee rows, at an everyday posture; the score counts contact per pose and does not see its depth or place. Bench(110,360) exact frozen: 10 contact poses (roller-longdyad 2, sidecar-longdyad 4), summed depth 44.0 mm (lead 6.23), deepest -12.0 mm at (plane 15, elev 165, axial -60). Five of the 10 are the side raise, scapular-plane abduction 90-105 with axial 15-45: (-15,105,15) -5.86, (-15,90,45) -4.42, (0,90,45) -3.01, (0,105,15) -2.85, (15,90,30) -0.71 mm, hub 2's crown. Held out: 26 contact poses plus 12 part clashes (roller-longdyad 10 + 0, sidecar-longdyad 10 + 5). Each contact pose is charged (about 0.54 gap points), so the number is honest; but the 2 mm / 3 mm advantage of this design (21 / 95 taken poses under 2 / 3 mm vs 30 / 133 for roller-longdyad) is partly bought by the poses where metal goes into the skin dropping out of the taken set.

reason: K is scored at its slaved value, held there by one clock-spring cap that force-closes two rolling pairs (the hub-2 lobe follower and the MR63ZZ roller on the conjugate flank). The verifier adds that K rests on its spring stop A on 499 of 863 held-out taken poses (58 %), so stop-A hold under gravity and arm load carries most of the workspace. Lift-off and pressure angle are checked only kinematically; no dynamics judge (R17) has run on this design (pick1's spring-held K lagged 9.3 deg at 0.08 N.m). This covers G2 (stiff spring) and G3 (cuff twist), both unmeasured. The slaved-coordinate coupling in judge/dynamics.py is the instrument, before CAD.

reason: The sample-weighted in-band share rises when more metal is added in band, without any out-of-band metal moving closer (the inverse of S2). This design's E strap carries 132 samples at 0.934 in band (lE 82.3 mm, searched in 35-95) and the bracket 105 at 0.997 (lc 29.9), against 104 / 85 on roller-longdyad and 104 / 95 on the lead; they dilute hub 3 (0.505 in band, median 13.9 mm) and link 2 (0.71). Arithmetic on the re-wear's per-part counts: with the sibling's E and bracket sample counts the in-band would be 0.8871 instead of 0.8907 (0.8905 scored; the per-part shares are rounded), worth up to 0.36 gap points (0.13 for the E strap alone; 0.24 at the lead's counts). The verifier's own --head wear shows the same direction: adding the roller-pin head and the lug edge strip as metal lowers the gap from 21.07 to 20.95 (roller-longdyad's 'envelope-corrected' 18.56 < 18.67 likewise). Small, and it does not change any ranking; the parts are real metal at true size, sampled at the standard spacing. Proposed catalogue entry S6 in the report.

reason: The design doc's 'New knowledge' 2 still credits the deleted knee for the small fast-to-frozen penalty: '+4.4 here vs +8.4-9.0 for the knee rows'. Those knee rows were searched on the plain or 1 mm gap (the lead went 10.30 fast -> 18.91 frozen). This design was searched on the 2 mm objective; the knee row with the same drive, wrapper and objective, roller-longdyad, pays +5.48 (13.19 -> 18.67) fast-to-frozen and +5.06 bench-to-held (this design +4.37 and +3.52). So the knee's share of the over-fit is about 1.1-1.5 points; the rest is the search objective (already a CLAUDE.md lesson). The verifier's appendix did not correct it. Not yet in FINDINGS or ROUNDS, but a planner reading the doc would delete knees for robustness on a confounded comparison.
